$comment: Generic rule registry: the engine's rules and the default working process. A project adds its own rules, paths and checkers in <workspace>/.devcontainer/harness/rules.json (seeded by dcc init from template/harness/); the engine merges the two — project rules with the same id replace generic ones, `disabled` removes ids, `protected_paths` extend, `phases` keys override, `project` is the project's own block. class: enforce = a control blocks it | verify = a checker tests the artifact | approve = a human decides | advise = prose only. check.builtin/regex/paths are handled by the hooks; check.run names a checker ({checkers} = generic dir, {project} = the overlay dir). trigger may be a string or an array; `gate` means harness check runs it on demand.

phases.$comment: The default working process: brainstorm and discussion (markdown only) -> plan (committed, ponytail-reviewed) -> review by the operator -> approval (a token only the operator can write) -> implement. A project narrows plan_glob, ticket_regex and allow_write.

preconditions.plan: a ticket reference (harness phase plan --ticket <repo>#<n>): every piece of work has a ticket
preconditions.review: the plan file exists under plan_glob, is committed, has no uncommitted changes, and the agent declares the ponytail review (--ponytail-reviewed)
preconditions.implement: an approval token whose content is the committed blob hash of the plan (dcc approve <plan> [--scope <glob>…] on the host); a plan edited after approval drops the phase back to review

rules.source: the operator's working process
rules.text: Writes are allowed only where the current phase permits. The phase advances through harness phase; implement needs the operator's approval token.

rules.source: operator's rule; incident 2026-07-21 (a plan approved in chat, written down afterwards)
rules.text: Code edits happen in phase implement only, which needs a committed plan file and the operator's approval token.

rules.source: operator's rule: plan approval in a conversation is not permission to implement
rules.text: Plan approval is a token the operator writes on the host. Without it the phase stays review and code writes are denied.

rules.source: operator's rule: keep changes scoped to the requested project
rules.text: In phase implement, writes stay inside the scope the operator gave with the approval (dcc approve <plan> --scope <glob>…) plus what phase review allows (the planning markdown: plans, DONE, archive); default scope is the whole workspace.

rules.source: operator's rule; incident 2026-07-22 (add -A swept another session's edits into a commit)
rules.text: Stage exact paths. Never git add -A/--all/-u/. or git commit -a.

rules.source: operator's rule; incident 2026-07-17 (a cd did not persist between calls; a commit landed on the wrong repo's main)
rules.text: Every mutating git command names its repo with -C /absolute/path.

rules.source: operator's rule: never disable signing; harness self-protection
rules.text: Never --no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, or a hooksPath/gpgsign override.

rules.source: operator's release convention: main goes to production through a Release PR
rules.text: Never push to production. Open a 'Release: …' PR from main and merge it.

rules.source: operator's rule: on push failure stop and hand over, never swap the transport
rules.text: Do not rewrite remotes, push to an explicit URL, or change the credential helper. On failure, stop and hand over.

rules.source: operator's rule; incident 2026-08-22 (45 PR bodies and 162 commit messages carried session links)
rules.text: No claude.ai session links, Co-Authored-By: Claude, or 'Generated with Claude Code' in anything that reaches GitHub.

rules.source: operator's ticket workflow: create and change tickets only through the project's scripts; raw gh for comments, milestones, body edits and transfers
rules.text: Ticket create/close/status changes go through the project's ticket scripts. Raw gh is for comments, milestones, body edits and transfers only. (Disable in a project without such scripts.)

rules.source: operator's ticket workflow: after any ticket change run the consistency check and fix or flag what it reports
rules.text: A session that changed tickets cannot end before the ticket check ran clean afterwards.

rules.source: operator's rule; credentials were burned once because secret values passed through a transcript
rules.text: Secret values never pass through the session: no gh secret set, sops, age, or SQL password changes. Hand the operator the commands.

rules.source: operator's rule; incident 2026-08-22 (a replacement database was installed instead of asking)
rules.text: When the dev database is unreachable, stop and ask. Never install or start a replacement database.

rules.source: harness self-protection: policy files, workflows, the agent's own settings. A project extends this with protected_paths.
rules.text: These paths are read-only for the agent. The guarantee is the read-only bind mount in devcontainer.json; this hook is the early feedback.

rules.source: operator's rule: a Release PR merges the tip of main at merge time, not the snapshot at opening
rules.text: Before merging a Release PR, list what main gained since it was opened and ask for the operator's approval; the token is bound to the PR head SHA.

rules.source: operator's rule
rules.text: ponytail-review runs over the plan before implementation; trims are folded in. Declared with --ponytail-reviewed; no mechanical proof.
rules.status: declaration recorded in the run state

rules.source: operator's rule
rules.text: If you implement code, do not assume things, ask.

rules.source: operator's rule
rules.text: Verify library behavior against the official docs for the pinned version before relying on it.

rules.source: operator's rule
rules.text: Do not over-implement or over-engineer. Use what exists or ask.

rules.source: operator's rule
rules.text: Focused tests for the change, then broader ones across boundaries.

rules.source: operator's rule
rules.text: Plans use Simplified Technical English and carry exact paths, identifiers and commands so an agent can execute them without extra lookup.
